content: Light griefs are loquacious, but the great are dumb.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. We spend enormous energy trying to present a sanitized, perfect version of ourselves to the world. But whatever emotions or desires we push into the dark don't disappear; they run our lives from behind the curtain.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. True maturity isn't pretending you have no dark corners—it is having the honesty and courage to look at your jealousy, fear, and anger in the daylight so they no longer control your actions.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
